threatCategories.label: Prompt Injection
threatCategories.whatItMeans: Untrusted text may influence system instructions or tool decisions.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: Prompt assembly, system prompts, user input, and missing sanitization or boundaries.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: A crafted instruction can redirect the agent from its intended task into unsafe execution.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Separate system and user content, sanitize inputs, constrain tools, and verify execution requests before action.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: A2SPA helps by requiring signed execution intent before a prompt-influenced tool call can run.

threatCategories.label: Memory Poisoning
threatCategories.whatItMeans: Agent memory can retain stale, sensitive, or attacker-influenced context.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: Persistent memory, vector stores, session history, missing TTL, or no context clearing.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: Poisoned context can steer future decisions long after the original interaction.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Set TTLs, scope memory to sessions, clear context after tasks, and validate memory writes.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: A2SPA reduces execution impact by requiring fresh authorization even if memory is poisoned.

threatCategories.label: Tool Misuse
threatCategories.whatItMeans: The agent can call tools that change data, money, infrastructure, or external systems.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: Tool lists, function calls, invoke/execute paths, broad permissions, or wildcard tools.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: Tool calls convert model output into real business actions.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Use allowlisted tools, per-tool scopes, approval gates for sensitive actions, and audit logging.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: A2SPA is directly relevant because it authorizes the intended tool action before execution.

threatCategories.label: Privilege Compromise
threatCategories.whatItMeans: The agent may hold more authority than the task requires.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: Admin/all/wildcard permissions, broad scopes, privileged credentials, or missing least privilege.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: A compromised agent can escalate from one task into account-wide or infrastructure-wide impact.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Apply least privilege, split duties, rotate secrets, and bind tools to narrow scopes.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: A2SPA can bind signed authorization to an explicit scope and action.

threatCategories.label: Resource Overload
threatCategories.whatItMeans: The agent may consume unbounded tokens, API calls, queue jobs, or infrastructure resources.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: Missing rate limits, timeouts, token budgets, retry caps, or max call counts.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: Runaway agents can create outages, cost spikes, and denial-of-service conditions.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Add rate limits, token budgets, timeouts, retry caps, and circuit breakers.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: A2SPA can make each execution auditable, but resource controls still need explicit limits.

threatCategories.label: Intent Breaking
threatCategories.whatItMeans: The agent may drift from approved user or business intent.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: Goal instructions, prompt override language, jailbreak patterns, or missing intent verification.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: An agent can complete the wrong task while appearing successful.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Validate requested action intent, constrain allowed goals, and require approval for sensitive deviations.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: A2SPA signs intended execution payloads so execution can be checked against approved intent.

threatCategories.label: Identity Spoofing
threatCategories.whatItMeans: The execution boundary may not prove which agent or caller requested an action.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: Agent identity, caller fields, service accounts, or missing signed identity checks.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: Spoofed identity lets rogue callers inherit trusted agent authority.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Verify agent identity, bind identity to the signed payload, and reject unknown callers.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: A2SPA helps by binding action, identity, nonce, and timestamp into signed authorization evidence.

threatCategories.label: Command Injection
threatCategories.whatItMeans: Untrusted input may reach a shell or command execution path.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: exec/spawn/subprocess/os.system, shell=true, or command strings built from request input.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: Command injection can become remote code execution and credential theft.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Avoid shell execution, validate arguments, use allowlisted commands, and pass args as arrays.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: A2SPA can authorize the intended operation, but command safety must be enforced at the tool boundary.

threatCategories.label: Supply Chain
threatCategories.whatItMeans: Dependencies, remote scripts, or plugin sources may change without review.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: Unpinned versions, remote install scripts, dynamic imports, or plugin dependencies.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: A dependency compromise can silently alter agent behavior or steal secrets.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Pin versions, verify integrity, review plugins, and use lockfiles or signed artifacts.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: A2SPA limits unauthorized execution impact, but dependency integrity still needs supply-chain controls.

threatCategories.label: Agent Communication Poisoning
threatCategories.whatItMeans: Messages between agents or systems may carry untrusted instructions.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: Delegation, handoffs, webhooks, message buses, or subagent communication.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: A poisoned message can propagate unsafe instructions across agent chains.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Scope delegated authority, validate messages, sign handoffs, and audit inter-agent actions.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: A2SPA can sign inter-agent execution requests and verify them at each boundary.

threatCategories.label: Replay Attacks
threatCategories.whatItMeans: A previously valid execution request may be reused.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: Nonce, idempotency key, timestamp, expiry validation, or missing replay controls.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: Captured requests can trigger repeated payments, deployments, or data changes.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Require unique nonces, mark them used, enforce timestamps, and reject expired requests.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: Nonce and timestamp validation are core A2SPA readiness evidence.

threatCategories.label: Version Drift
threatCategories.whatItMeans: Runtime model or agent versions may change without controlled review.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: Model names, versions, unpinned model config, or missing version metadata.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: Model drift can change decisions, prompts, and tool usage behavior between releases.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Pin model/version config, record release metadata, and re-scan after model changes.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: A2SPA receipts can include model/version metadata for accountability.

threatCategories.label: Auditability
threatCategories.whatItMeans: Execution may not leave enough evidence to investigate or prove what happened.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: Audit logs, receipts, request IDs, traces, or missing structured execution records.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: Without non-repudiation, incidents become difficult to reconstruct and defend.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Write signed/auditable execution receipts with identity, action, timestamp, and result.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: A2SPA audit receipts support accountability at execution boundaries.

threatCategories.label: Rogue Agent
threatCategories.whatItMeans: Unknown or malicious agents may be able to join the workflow.
threatCategories.evidencePattern: Agent registration, plugin onboarding, dynamic agents, or missing identity verification.
threatCategories.whyItMatters: A rogue agent can inherit trust and execute actions as part of the system.
threatCategories.recommendedFix: Verify agent identity during onboarding, approve allowed agents, and bind permissions to identity.
threatCategories.a2spaImpact: A2SPA can require verified agent identity before execution authorization is accepted.

findings.title: Missing cryptographic signature
findings.whatIsWrong: No cryptographic signature was detected in this agent configuration.
findings.whyItMatters: Without a signature, there is no proof the payload is authentic before it triggers real-world actions. Any intercepted or modified request will execute without detection.
findings.capabilityImpact: An attacker who can intercept or forge a request can trigger this agent's actions without being caught.

findings.title: Missing nonce validation
findings.whatIsWrong: No nonce or replay protection token was detected.
findings.whyItMatters: Without a unique per-request token, replay attacks become trivial. An attacker can capture and re-execute any valid request.
findings.capabilityImpact: A captured request (e.g. a payment or deployment) could be replayed to repeat the same action.

findings.title: Missing timestamp enforcement
findings.whatIsWrong: No timestamp or expiry validation was detected.
findings.whyItMatters: Expired payloads remain valid indefinitely and can trigger execution long after the intended window.
findings.capabilityImpact: A request captured today could still trigger a real action months from now.

findings.title: Missing fail-closed enforcement
findings.whatIsWrong: No fail-closed pattern detected. Verification failures may still allow execution.
findings.whyItMatters: Without a hard block on verification failure, a failed check is just a warning. Execution proceeds regardless.
findings.capabilityImpact: A broken or bypassed check does not stop the agent — it keeps acting as if nothing was wrong.

findings.title: Rogue agent onboarding risk
findings.whatIsWrong: The agent appears to register, onboard, or invoke remote agents/plugins without visible identity verification.
findings.whyItMatters: Unknown agents can inherit trusted tool access. A malicious or spoofed agent can execute actions as if it were approved.
findings.capabilityImpact: An unverified agent or plugin could be onboarded and inherit this system's trusted access.

findings.title: Missing audit logging
findings.whatIsWrong: No audit logging or execution tracking detected.
findings.whyItMatters: Without an audit trail, forensic investigation after a failure or breach is impossible. Compliance requirements cannot be met.
findings.capabilityImpact: If this agent is misused, there may be no record of who or what triggered the action.

findings.title: No execution rate limiting
findings.whatIsWrong: No rate limiting, token budget, or call quota detected.
findings.whyItMatters: Agents without execution budgets can exhaust API quotas, generate unbounded costs, and create denial-of-service conditions.
findings.capabilityImpact: A loop or malicious instruction could run this agent's actions an unbounded number of times.
